description: Zirconium is a chemical element with symbol Zr and atomic number 40. It is a lustrous transition metal with a greyish-white color that is solid at room temperature, ductile, malleable, and corrosion-resistant.
uses: Zirconium and its alloys are mainly used as a refractory and opacifier. Zirconium alloys are used to clad nuclear fuel rods due to their low neutron absorption and corrosion resistance, in space vehicles and turbine blades for high heat resistance, in flashbulbs, dental implants and prosthetics, deodorant, and water purification systems.
characteristics: Zirconium is a soft metal that is highly resistant to corrosion by alkalis, acids, and salt water, though it dissolves in hydrochloric and sulfuric acid in the presence of fluorine. It has a melting point of 1855°C and a boiling point of 4409°C. In powder form it is highly flammable, but the solid form is much less prone to ignition.
